verses.text: 1:1After Alexander son of Philip, the Macedonian who came from the land of Kittim, had defeated Darius king of the Persians and Medes, he became king in his place, having first ruled over Greece.
1:2He waged many wars, took possession of strongholds, and slaughtered kings of the earth.
1:3He passed through to the ends of the earth and took the spoils of a multitude of nations. The earth became quiet before him; he was exalted, and his heart was lifted up.
1:4He gathered an exceedingly strong army and ruled over countries, nations, and rulers; they became tributary to him.
1:5After this he fell upon his bed and knew that he was dying.
1:6He summoned his distinguished officers, who had been brought up with him from his youth, and divided his kingdom among them while he was still alive.
1:7Alexander reigned twelve years, and he died.
1:8His officers took power, each in his own place.
1:9They all put on diadems after his death, and their sons after them for many years; they multiplied evils on the earth.
1:10From them came a sinful root: Antiochus Epiphanes, son of King Antiochus, who had been a hostage in Rome. He became king in the one hundred and thirty-seventh year of the kingdom of the Greeks.

1:11In those days lawless sons came out of Israel and persuaded many, saying, “Let us go and make a covenant with the nations around us, because since we separated ourselves from them, many evils have overtaken us.”
1:12The proposal was good in their eyes.
1:13Some of the people eagerly went to the king, and he gave them authority to follow the ordinances of the nations.
1:14They built a gymnasium in Jerusalem according to the customs of the nations
1:15and made foreskins for themselves. They abandoned the holy covenant, yoked themselves to the nations, and sold themselves to do evil.
1:16The kingdom was established before Antiochus, and he planned to reign over the land of Egypt so that he might rule both kingdoms.
1:17He entered Egypt with a heavy force, with chariots, elephants, cavalry, and a great fleet,
1:18and waged war against Ptolemy king of Egypt. Ptolemy was driven back before him and fled, and many fell wounded.
1:19They seized the fortified cities in the land of Egypt, and he took the spoils of the land of Egypt.
1:20After striking Egypt, Antiochus returned in the one hundred and forty-third year. He went up against Israel and came up to Jerusalem with a heavy force.
1:21He arrogantly entered the sanctuary and took the golden altar, the lampstand for light and all its utensils,
1:22the table of presentation, the libation vessels, the bowls, the golden censers, the curtain, the crowns, and the gold ornament on the front of the temple. He stripped everything off.
1:23He took the silver, the gold, the precious vessels, and the hidden treasures that he found.
1:24Having taken everything, he went away to his own land. He committed bloodshed and spoke with great arrogance.
1:25Great mourning came upon Israel in every place where they lived.
1:26Rulers and elders groaned; young women and young men grew weak, and the beauty of women was changed.
1:27Every bridegroom took up a lament, and the bride sitting in her bridal chamber mourned.
1:28The earth shook over its inhabitants, and the whole house of Jacob put on shame.
1:29After two full years, the king sent a chief collector of tribute to the cities of Judah. He came to Jerusalem with a heavy force.
1:30He spoke peaceful words to them deceitfully, and they trusted him. Then he suddenly fell upon the city, struck it a great blow, and destroyed many people of Israel.
1:31He took the spoils of the city and burned it with fire. He demolished its houses and its surrounding walls.
1:32They took the women and children captive and took possession of the livestock.
1:33They fortified the city of David with a great, strong wall and strong towers, and it became their citadel.
1:34They stationed there a sinful nation, lawless men, and strengthened themselves in it.
1:35They stored weapons and food, gathered the spoils of Jerusalem, and deposited them there. They became a great trap.
1:36It became an ambush against the sanctuary and an evil adversary to Israel continually.
1:37They poured out innocent blood around the sanctuary and defiled the sanctuary.
1:38Because of them the inhabitants of Jerusalem fled, and she became a dwelling of foreigners. She became foreign to those born in her, and her children abandoned her.
1:39Her sanctuary was laid waste like a wilderness; her festivals were turned into mourning, her sabbaths into reproach, and her honour into contempt.
1:40In proportion to her glory, her dishonour multiplied, and her exaltation was turned into mourning.
1:41The king wrote to his whole kingdom that all should become one people
1:42and that each should abandon his own customs. All the nations accepted the king’s command.
1:43Many from Israel consented to his worship, sacrificed to idols, and profaned the sabbath.
1:44The king sent letters by messengers to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, ordering them to follow customs foreign to the land,
1:45to prevent whole burnt offerings, sacrifice, and libation in the sanctuary, to profane sabbaths and festivals,
1:46to defile the sanctuary and holy people,
1:47to build pagan altars, sacred precincts, and shrines for idols, and to sacrifice pigs and unclean livestock,
1:48to leave their sons uncircumcised, and to make themselves abominable through every uncleanness and profanation,
1:49so that they would forget the law and change all the ordinances.
1:50Whoever did not act according to the king’s command was to die.
1:51In accordance with all these commands he wrote to his whole kingdom. He appointed overseers over all the people and commanded the cities of Judah to sacrifice, city by city.
1:52Many of the people gathered to them, everyone who abandoned the law, and they did evil in the land.
1:53They drove Israel into hiding in all their places of refuge.
1:54On the fifteenth day of Chislev, in the one hundred and forty-fifth year, he built an abomination of desolation upon the altar. They built pagan altars in the surrounding cities of Judah.
1:55At the doors of the houses and in the squares they burned incense.
1:56They tore apart the books of the law that they found and burned them with fire.
1:57Whenever a book of the covenant was found in someone’s possession, or anyone consented to the law, the king’s decree put him to death.
1:58By their power they dealt in this way with Israelites found in the cities, month after month.
1:59On the twenty-fifth day of the month they offered sacrifice on the pagan altar that stood upon the altar.
1:60According to the decree, they put to death the women who had circumcised their children,
1:61hanging the infants from their necks; they also killed their households and those who had circumcised them.
1:62Many in Israel stood firm and fortified themselves against eating unclean things.
1:63They chose to die so that they would not be defiled by foods or profane the holy covenant, and they died.
1:64Very great wrath came upon Israel.
2:1In those days Mattathias son of John son of Simeon, a priest of the sons of Joarib, arose from Jerusalem and settled in Modein.
2:2He had five sons: John, called Gaddi;
2:3Simon, called Thassi;
2:4Judas, called Maccabeus;
2:5Eleazar, called Avaran; and Jonathan, called Apphous.
2:6He saw the blasphemies being committed in Judah and Jerusalem

2:7and said, “Alas for me! Why was I born to see the ruin of my people and the ruin of the holy city, and to sit there while she was given into the hand of enemies, the sanctuary into the hand of foreigners?
2:8Her temple has become like a man without honour.
2:10What nation has not taken possession of her royal places and seized her spoils?

2:11All her adornment was taken away;
she that was free became a slave.
2:12Behold! Our holy places, our beauty, and our glory have been laid waste, and the nations have profaned them.
2:13Why should we live any longer?”
2:14Mattathias and his sons tore their garments, put on sackcloth, and mourned greatly.
2:15The king’s officials who were compelling apostasy came to the city of Modein to make the people sacrifice.
2:16Many from Israel came to them, and Mattathias and his sons gathered.
2:17The king’s officials addressed Mattathias, saying, “You are a ruler, honoured and great in this city, supported by sons and brothers.

2:18Now be the first to come forward and carry out the king’s decree, as all the nations, the men of Judah, and those left in Jerusalem have done. You and your sons shall be among the king’s Friends, and you and your sons shall be honoured with silver, gold, and many gifts.”
2:19Mattathias answered in a loud voice, “Even if all the nations within the king’s realm obey him, each abandoning the worship of his fathers, and have chosen his commands,
2:20I and my sons and my brothers will walk in the covenant of our fathers.
2:21Far be it from us to abandon the law and the ordinances!
2:22We will not obey the king’s words by turning aside from our worship to the right or to the left.”
2:23When he finished speaking these words, a Jewish man came forward in the sight of everyone to sacrifice upon the pagan altar in Modein, according to the king’s decree.
2:24Mattathias saw and burned with zeal; his inward parts trembled. He gave vent to anger according to the judgment, ran forward, and slaughtered him upon the altar.
2:25At that time he also killed the king’s officer who was compelling sacrifice, and he pulled down the altar.
2:26He was zealous for the law, just as Phinehas had acted toward Zimri son of Salom.
2:27Mattathias cried out in the city with a loud voice, “Let everyone who is zealous for the law and upholds the covenant come out after me!”
2:28He and his sons fled to the mountains and abandoned everything they had in the city.
2:29Then many who sought righteousness and judgment went down into the wilderness to settle there,
2:30with their sons, their wives, and their livestock, because the evils had become severe against them.
2:31It was reported to the king’s men and the forces in Jerusalem, the city of David, that men who had rejected the king’s command had gone down into hiding places in the wilderness.
2:32Many pursued them, overtook them, encamped against them, and prepared for battle against them on the sabbath day.
2:33They said to them, “Enough of this! Come out and act according to the king’s command, and you shall live.”
2:34They said, “We will not come out, nor will we carry out the king’s command by profaning the sabbath day.”
2:35They hurried into battle against them.
2:36But they did not answer them, throw a stone at them, or block the hiding places,
2:37saying, “Let us all die in our integrity. Heaven and earth bear witness concerning us that you are destroying us without judgment.”
2:38They attacked them in battle on the sabbath. They died, together with their wives, their children, and their livestock—about a thousand human lives.
2:39Mattathias and his friends learned of it and mourned for them greatly.
2:40Each said to his neighbour, “If we all do as our brothers have done and do not fight the nations for our lives and our ordinances, they will now quickly destroy us from the earth.”
2:41That day they resolved, saying, “If anyone comes against us for battle on the sabbath day, we will fight against him, and we will certainly not all die as our brothers died in the hiding places.”
2:42Then a company of Hasideans gathered to them, strong warriors from Israel, everyone who willingly offered himself for the law.
2:43All who were fleeing from the evils joined them and became their support.
2:44They organized an army and struck sinners in their anger and lawless men in their wrath. The rest fled to the nations for safety.
2:45Mattathias and his friends went around and pulled down the pagan altars.
2:46They forcibly circumcised all the uncircumcised boys whom they found within the borders of Israel.
2:47They pursued the sons of arrogance, and the work prospered in their hands.
2:48They took the law out of the hand of the nations and the kings, and they did not allow the sinner to gain a horn.
2:49When the days drew near for Mattathias to die, he said to his sons, “Now arrogance and rebuke have grown strong—a time of overthrow and furious wrath.
2:50Now, children, be zealous for the law and give your lives for the covenant of our fathers.
2:51Remember the deeds of the fathers that they did in their generations, and receive great glory and an everlasting name.
2:52Was not Abraham found faithful in testing, and was it not reckoned to him as righteousness?
2:53Joseph, in the time of his distress, kept the commandment and became lord of Egypt.
2:54Phinehas our father, by burning with zeal, received a covenant of everlasting priesthood.
2:55Joshua, by fulfilling the word, became a judge in Israel.
2:56Caleb, by bearing witness in the assembly, received an inheritance of land.
2:57David, through his mercy, inherited a royal throne for ever.
2:58Elijah, by burning with zeal for the law, was taken up into heaven.
2:59Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael trusted and were saved from the flame.
2:60Daniel, in his integrity, was rescued from the mouth of lions.
2:61So consider it from generation to generation: all who hope in Him will not fail.
2:62Do not fear the words of a sinful man, for his glory will become dung and worms.
2:63Today he shall be exalted, and tomorrow he shall not be found, for he has returned to his dust, and his thought shall perish.
2:64Children, be courageous and be strong in the law, because through it you shall be glorified.
2:65Behold, Simon your brother—I know that he is a man of counsel. Listen to him all your days; he will be your father.
2:66Judas Maccabeus has been a strong warrior from his youth. He will be your army commander and will fight the battle of peoples.
2:67Gather to yourselves all who carry out the law, and exact vengeance for your people.
2:68Repay the nations what is due to them, and attend to the law’s command.”
2:69Then he blessed them and was gathered to his fathers.
2:70He died in the one hundred and forty-sixth year and was buried in the tombs of his fathers in Modein. All Israel lamented him with a great lament.
3:1His son Judas, called Maccabeus, arose in his place.
3:2All his brothers and everyone who had joined his father helped him, and they fought Israel’s war with gladness.

3:3He spread glory for his people,
put on a breastplate like a giant,
and girded himself with his weapons of war;
he waged battles, shielding the army with his sword.

3:4In his deeds he was like a lion,
like a young lion roaring over prey.
3:5He searched out and pursued the lawless, and burned those who troubled his people.
3:8He passed through the cities of Judah, destroyed the ungodly out of her, and turned wrath away from Israel.
3:9His name reached to the end of the earth, and he gathered those who were perishing.
3:10Apollonius gathered nations and a great force from Samaria to fight against Israel.
3:11Judas learned of it, went out to meet him, struck him, and killed him. Many fell wounded, and the survivors fled.
3:12They took their spoils. Judas took Apollonius’s sword and fought with it all his days.
3:13Seron, commander of the Syrian force, heard that Judas had gathered a body of men, an assembly of faithful men who were with him and went out to war.
3:14He said, “I will make a name for myself and be honoured in the kingdom. I will fight Judas and those with him who despise the king’s command.”
3:15He set out again, and a strong army of ungodly men went up with him to help him take vengeance on the sons of Israel.
3:16He approached the ascent of Beth-horon, and Judas went out to meet him with only a few men.
3:17When they saw the army coming to meet them, they said to Judas, “How can we, being so few, fight such a strong multitude? We are exhausted, having eaten nothing today.”
3:18Judas said, “It is easy for many to be shut into the hands of a few. Before Heaven there is no difference between saving by many or by few.
3:19For victory in battle does not lie in the size of an army; strength comes from heaven.
3:20They come against us in an abundance of arrogance and lawlessness to destroy us, our wives, and our children, and to plunder us.
3:21But we are fighting for our lives and our customs.
3:22He Himself will crush them before us. Do not be afraid of them.”
3:23When he finished speaking, he rushed upon them suddenly, and Seron and his army were crushed before him.
3:24They pursued him down the descent of Beth-horon as far as the plain. About eight hundred of their men fell, and the rest fled into the land of the Philistines.
3:25Then fear of Judas and his brothers began, and terror fell upon the nations around them.
3:26His name reached the king, and the nations recounted the battles of Judas.
3:27When King Antiochus heard these reports, he became furious. He sent and gathered all the forces of his kingdom, an exceedingly strong army.
3:28He opened his treasury, gave the forces a year’s pay, and commanded them to be ready for every need.

3:29He saw that the money in the treasuries was exhausted and the revenues of the country were small because of the dissension and disaster he had brought upon the land by removing the customs that had existed from the earliest days.
3:30He feared that he would not have enough, as on former occasions, for expenses and for the gifts that he had previously given with a lavish hand, surpassing the kings before him.
3:31He was greatly perplexed in his soul and resolved to go to Persia, collect the revenues of the countries, and gather much silver.
3:32He left Lysias, an honoured man of royal lineage, in charge of the king’s affairs from the Euphrates River to the borders of Egypt
3:33and to bring up his son Antiochus until he returned.
3:34He handed over to him half the forces and the elephants, and instructed him concerning everything he wished, including the inhabitants of Judea and Jerusalem:
3:35he was to send an army against them to crush and remove Israel’s strength and the remnant of Jerusalem, and to remove their memory from the place.
3:36He was to settle foreigners throughout all their territory and allot their land to them.

3:37The king took the remaining half of the forces and set out from Antioch, his royal city, in the one hundred and forty-seventh year. He crossed the Euphrates River and travelled through the upper countries.
3:38Lysias selected Ptolemy son of Dorymenes, Nicanor, and Gorgias, capable men among the king’s Friends.
3:39He sent with them forty thousand men and seven thousand cavalry to enter the land of Judah and destroy it, according to the king’s command.
3:40He set out with all their force, and they came and encamped near Emmaus in the lowland.

3:41The merchants of the country heard their reputation, took a very great quantity of silver and gold, along with shackles, and came to the camp to buy the sons of Israel as slaves. A force from Syria and the land of foreigners joined them.
3:42Judas and his brothers saw that the evils had multiplied and that the forces were encamping within their borders. They learned the king’s commands to bring destruction and an end upon the people.
3:43Each said to his neighbour, “Let us restore our people’s fallen state and fight for our people and the holy places.”
3:44The assembly gathered to prepare for war, to pray, and to ask for mercy and compassion.

3:45Jerusalem was uninhabited like a wilderness. None of those born in her went in or out; the sanctuary was being trampled, and foreigners were in the citadel, a lodging for the nations. Delight was removed from Jacob, and flute and lyre ceased.
3:46They gathered and came to Mizpah opposite Jerusalem, because formerly Mizpah had been a place of prayer for Israel.
3:47They fasted that day, put on sackcloth, placed ashes on their heads, and tore their garments.
3:48They unrolled the book of the law concerning the matters for which the nations consulted the likenesses of their idols.
3:49They brought the priestly garments, the firstfruits, and the tithes, and brought forward the Nazirites who had completed their days.
3:50They cried aloud to Heaven, saying, “What shall we do with these, and where shall we take them,
3:51when Thy holy places have been trampled and profaned, and Thy priests are in mourning and humiliation?
3:52Behold! The nations have gathered against us to destroy us. Thou knowest what they are planning against us.
3:53How can we stand before them unless Thou help us?”
3:54They sounded the trumpets and cried out with a loud voice.
3:55After this Judas appointed leaders of the people: commanders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
3:56He told those building houses, those betrothed to wives, those planting vineyards, and the fearful to return, each to his own house, according to the law.
3:57The army set out, and they encamped south of Emmaus.
3:58Judas said, “Gird yourselves and become men of strength. Be ready in the morning to fight these nations that have gathered against us to destroy us and our holy places.
3:59It is better for us to die in battle than to look upon the evils suffered by our nation and the holy places.
3:60But whatever the will in heaven may be, that He will do.”
4:1Gorgias took five thousand men and a thousand picked cavalry, and the army set out by night
4:2to fall upon the camp of the Jews and strike them suddenly. Men from the citadel served as his guides.
4:3Judas heard of it, and he and the mighty men set out to strike the king’s force at Emmaus,
4:4while the forces were still scattered away from the camp.
4:5Gorgias came to Judas’s camp by night and found no one. He searched for them in the mountains, saying, “They are fleeing from us.”
4:6At daybreak Judas appeared on the plain with three thousand men, though they did not have the protective equipment and swords they wanted.
4:7They saw a strong army of nations, armoured, with cavalry surrounding it; these men were trained for war.
4:8Judas said to the men with him, “Do not fear their multitude or lose courage before their assault.
4:9Remember how our fathers were saved at the Red Sea when Pharaoh pursued them with an army.
4:10Now let us cry to Heaven: perhaps He will favour us, remember the covenant of the fathers, and crush this army before us today.
4:11Then all the nations will know that there is One who redeems and saves Israel.”
4:12The foreigners raised their eyes and saw them coming from the opposite side.
4:13They went out of the camp for battle, and Judas’s men sounded the trumpet.
4:14They engaged, and the nations were crushed and fled into the plain.
4:15All who were at the rear fell by the sword. They pursued them as far as Gazera and the plains of Idumea, Azotus, and Jamnia; about three thousand of their men fell.
4:16Judas and his force returned from pursuing them,
4:17and he said to the people, “Do not covet the spoils, because a battle lies before us.
4:18Gorgias and his force are in the mountain near us. Stand now against our enemies and fight them; afterward take the spoils freely.”
4:19While Judas was finishing these words, a detachment appeared, looking out from the mountain.
4:20They saw that their men had been routed and that the camp was being burned, for the visible smoke made plain what had happened.
4:21Seeing these things, they became exceedingly afraid. When they also saw Judas’s army on the plain ready for battle,
4:22they all fled into the land of foreigners.
4:23Judas returned to plunder the camp, and they took much gold and silver, blue cloth, sea-purple cloth, and great wealth.
4:24On their return they sang hymns and blessed Heaven: “For it is good, for His mercy is for ever.”
4:25A great deliverance came to Israel that day.
4:26Those foreigners who escaped came and reported to Lysias everything that had happened.
4:27When he heard it, he was confused and disheartened, because what he had wished had not happened to Israel, and what the king had commanded him had not come about.
4:28In the following year he assembled sixty thousand picked men and five thousand cavalry to make war on them.
4:29They came into Idumea and encamped at Beth-zur. Judas met them with ten thousand men.

4:30He saw the strong army and prayed, saying, “Blessed art Thou, Saviour of Israel, who didst crush the mighty man’s assault by the hand of Thy servant David, and didst deliver the foreigners’ army into the hands of Jonathan son of Saul and his armour-bearer.
4:31So shut this army into the hand of Thy people Israel, and let them be ashamed of their force and their cavalry.
4:32Give them cowardice; melt the boldness of their strength, and let them be shaken by their collapse.
4:33Bring them down by the sword of those who love Thee, and let all who know Thy name praise Thee with hymns.”
4:34They joined battle with one another. About five thousand men from Lysias’s army fell; they fell before them.

4:35Lysias saw the rout of his own formation, the courage that had arisen in Judas’s men, and how they were ready either to live or to die nobly. He withdrew to Antioch and recruited mercenaries in greater numbers to come again into Judea.
4:36Judas and his brothers said, “Behold! Our enemies have been crushed. Let us go up to cleanse the holy places and dedicate them anew.”
4:37The whole army gathered, and they went up to Mount Zion.
4:38They saw the sanctuary desolate, the altar profaned, the gates burned down, plants growing in the courts as in a thicket or on one of the mountains, and the chambers demolished.
4:39They tore their garments, lamented with a great lament, and put ashes on themselves.
4:40They fell face down upon the ground, sounded the signal trumpets, and cried to Heaven.
4:41Then Judas ordered men to fight those in the citadel until he had cleansed the holy places.
4:42He chose blameless priests devoted to the law.
4:43They cleansed the holy places and carried the stones of defilement to an unclean place.
4:44They deliberated what to do with the altar of whole burnt offering, which had been profaned.
4:45They considered it best to pull it down, so that it would not become a reproach to them because the nations had defiled it. They pulled down the altar
4:46and placed the stones on the mountain of the house in a suitable place until a prophet should come to give an answer about them.
4:47They took whole stones according to the law and built a new altar like the former one.
4:48They rebuilt the holy places and the interior of the house, and consecrated the courts.
4:49They made new holy vessels and brought the lampstand, the incense altar, and the table into the temple.
4:50They burned incense upon the altar and lit the lamps on the lampstand, and they shone in the temple.
4:51They placed loaves on the table and spread out the curtains. They completed all the works they had undertaken.
4:52They rose early in the morning on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month, which is the month of Chislev, in the one hundred and forty-eighth year.
4:53They offered sacrifice according to the law upon the new altar of whole burnt offerings that they had made.
4:54At the season and on the day on which the nations had profaned it, it was dedicated with songs, harps, lyres, and cymbals.
4:55All the people fell face down, worshiped, and blessed toward heaven the One who had prospered them.
4:56They celebrated the dedication of the altar for eight days, offered whole burnt offerings with gladness, and sacrificed a sacrifice of well-being and praise.
4:57They adorned the front of the temple with golden crowns and small shields, renewed the gateways and chambers, and fitted them with doors.
4:58There was exceedingly great gladness among the people, and the reproach of the nations was turned away.

4:59Judas, his brothers, and the whole assembly of Israel established that the days of the altar’s dedication should be celebrated at their proper season, year by year, for eight days beginning on the twenty-fifth of the month of Chislev, with gladness and joy.
4:60At that time they built high walls and strong towers around Mount Zion so that the nations could not come and trample them as they had done before.
4:61He stationed a force there to guard it, and fortified it to guard Beth-zur, so that the people would have a stronghold facing Idumea.
5:1When the nations round about heard that the altar had been rebuilt and the sanctuary dedicated as before, they became exceedingly angry.
5:2They resolved to remove the descendants of Jacob living among them, and began killing and destroying people.
5:3Judas fought against the sons of Esau in Idumea, in Akrabattene, because they were besieging Israel. He struck them a great blow, subdued them, and took their spoils.
5:4He remembered the evil of the sons of Baean, who had become a trap and a stumbling block for the people by ambushing them on the roads.
5:5He shut them into the towers, encamped against them, devoted them to destruction, and burned the towers with everyone inside.
5:6He crossed over against the sons of Ammon and found a strong force and many people, with Timothy as their leader.
5:7He engaged them in many battles. They were crushed before him, and he struck them.
5:8He seized Jazer and its daughter towns, then returned to Judea.
5:9The nations in Gilead gathered against the Israelites living in their territory to destroy them, and they fled into the stronghold of Dathema.
5:10They sent letters to Judas and his brothers, saying, “The nations around us have gathered against us to destroy us.
5:11They are preparing to come and seize the stronghold into which we fled, and Timothy is leading their force.
5:12Now, therefore, come and rescue us from their hand, because many of us have fallen.
5:13All our brothers in the region of Tobiah have been put to death. They have taken their wives, children, and belongings captive, and have destroyed about a thousand men there.”
5:14While the letters were still being read, other messengers arrived from Galilee with torn garments, reporting similar things.
5:15They said that people from Ptolemais, Tyre, and Sidon, and all Galilee of foreigners, had gathered against them “to consume us completely.”
5:16When Judas and the people heard these words, a great assembly gathered to deliberate what to do for their brothers who were in distress and under attack.
5:17Judas said to Simon his brother, “Choose men for yourself and go and deliver your brothers in Galilee. I and Jonathan my brother will go to Gilead.”
5:18He left Joseph son of Zechariah and Azariah, a leader of the people, with the remaining force in Judea to guard it.
5:19He commanded them, saying, “Take charge of this people, and do not engage the nations in battle until we return.”
5:20Three thousand men were assigned to Simon to go to Galilee, and eight thousand men to Judas for Gilead.
5:21Simon went to Galilee and engaged the nations in many battles. The nations were crushed before him,
5:22and he pursued them to the gate of Ptolemais. About three thousand men of the nations fell, and he took their spoils.
5:23He took those from Galilee and Arbattos, with their wives, children, and everything they had, and brought them into Judea with great gladness.
5:24Judas Maccabeus and Jonathan his brother crossed the Jordan and travelled a three-day journey in the wilderness.
5:25They met the Nabateans, who received them peacefully and recounted everything that had happened to their brothers in Gilead.
5:26Many of them had been confined in Bosora, Bosor in Alema, Chaspho, Maked, and Carnaim—all these cities were strong and large.
5:27They were also confined in the other cities of Gilead. The enemy had arranged to attack the strongholds the next day, seize them, and destroy all these people in one day.

5:28Judas and his army suddenly turned their route toward Bosora through the wilderness. He seized the city, killed every male with the edge of the sword, took all their spoils, and burned it with fire.
5:29He set out from there by night, and they travelled as far as the stronghold.
5:30In the morning they raised their eyes and saw a great people beyond counting, carrying ladders and siege engines to seize the stronghold and attacking its defenders.
5:31Judas saw that the battle had begun and that the city’s cry rose to heaven with trumpets and a loud shout.
5:32He said to the men of the force, “Fight today for our brothers!”
5:33He came out behind them in three divisions. They sounded the trumpets and cried out in prayer.
5:34Timothy’s army recognized that it was Maccabeus and fled before him. He struck them a great blow, and about eight thousand of their men fell that day.
5:35He turned aside to Alema, attacked it, seized it, killed every male in it, took its spoils, and burned it with fire.
5:36He set out from there and seized Chaspho, Maked, Bosor, and the other cities of Gilead.
5:37After these events Timothy gathered another army and encamped opposite Raphon, beyond the stream.
5:38Judas sent men to spy out the camp. They reported to him, saying, “All the nations around us have gathered to him, a very large force.
5:39They have hired Arabs to help them and are encamped beyond the stream, ready to come against you in battle.” Judas went to meet them.

5:40As Judas and his army approached the watercourse, Timothy said to his army commanders, “If he crosses over to us first, we will not be able to stand against him; he will surely prevail against us.
5:41But if he becomes afraid and encamps beyond the river, we will cross over to him and prevail against him.”
5:42When Judas approached the watercourse, he stationed the officers of the people at the stream and commanded them, saying, “Do not allow anyone to encamp; let everyone come into the battle.”
5:43He crossed over against them first, with all the people behind him. All the nations were crushed before them; they threw away their weapons and fled to the sacred precinct of Carnaim.
5:44They seized the city and burned the sacred precinct with everyone inside. Carnaim was overthrown, and they could no longer stand before Judas.
5:45Judas gathered all Israel in Gilead, from small to great, with their wives, their children, and their belongings—a very great company—to go into the land of Judah.
5:46They came as far as Ephron. It was a large, exceedingly strong city on the road, and there was no way to turn aside from it to the right or left, but only to pass through its midst.
5:47The people of the city shut them out and blocked the gates with stones.
5:48Judas sent to them with peaceful words, saying, “We will pass through your land to go to our land. No one will harm you; we will only pass through on foot.” But they would not open to him.
5:49Judas ordered a proclamation through the company that each should encamp in the place where he was.
5:50The men of the force encamped. He attacked the city all that day and all that night, and the city was given into his hand.
5:51He destroyed every male with the edge of the sword, uprooted the city, took its spoils, and passed through the city over the slain.
5:52They crossed the Jordan into the great plain opposite Beth-shan.
5:53Judas gathered those who lagged behind and encouraged the people along the whole road until he came into the land of Judah.
5:54They went up to Mount Zion with gladness and joy and presented whole burnt offerings, because none of them had fallen before they returned in peace.
5:55In the days when Judas and Jonathan were in the land of Gilead, and Simon his brother was in Galilee opposite Ptolemais,
5:56Joseph son of Zechariah and Azariah, commanders of the force, heard of their brave deeds and the warfare they had carried out.
5:57They said, “Let us also make a name for ourselves. Let us go and fight the nations around us.”
5:58They gave orders to the men of the force with them, and they marched against Jamnia.
5:59Gorgias and his men came out of the city to meet them in battle.
5:60Joseph and Azariah were routed and pursued to the borders of Judea. About two thousand men of the people of Israel fell that day.
5:61A great rout occurred among the people because they had not listened to Judas and his brothers, thinking to perform brave deeds.
5:62But they were not of the line of those men through whose hand the deliverance of Israel had been granted.
5:63The man Judas and his brothers were greatly honoured before all Israel and all the nations wherever their name was heard.
5:64People gathered to them, acclaiming them.
5:65Judas and his brothers went out and fought the sons of Esau in the southern land. He struck Hebron and its daughter towns, demolished its fortifications, and burned its towers all around.
5:66He set out to go into the land of foreigners and passed through Marisa.
5:67That day priests fell in battle because they wished to perform brave deeds and went out to battle without counsel.

5:68Judas turned aside to Azotus in the land of foreigners, pulled down their pagan altars, burned the carved images of their gods with fire, took the spoils of the cities, and returned to the land of Judah.
6:1King Antiochus was travelling through the upper countries when he heard that Elymais in Persia was a city renowned for wealth, silver, and gold.
6:2Its temple was exceedingly rich, and there were golden coverings, breastplates, and weapons left there by Alexander son of Philip, the Macedonian king who first reigned among the Greeks.
6:3He came and tried to seize the city and plunder it, but could not, because the people of the city learned of his plan.
6:4They resisted him in battle, and he fled and withdrew from there in great sorrow to return to Babylon.
6:5Someone came to Persia to report to him that the armies that had gone into the land of Judah had been routed;

6:6that Lysias had gone at first with a strong army but had been driven back before them; and that they had grown strong in weapons, power, and the many spoils they had taken from the armies they had cut down.
6:7They had pulled down the abomination he had built upon the altar in Jerusalem and surrounded the sanctuary with high walls as before, and also Beth-zur, his city.
6:8When the king heard these reports, he was astonished and greatly shaken. He fell upon his bed and became ill from sorrow, because things had not happened to him as he had intended.
6:9He remained there many days, for great sorrow came upon him again, and he judged that he was dying.
6:10He called all his Friends and said to them, “Sleep is departing from my eyes, and my heart has collapsed from anxiety.
6:11I said in my heart, ‘Into what distress and great storm have I come, in which I now find myself?’ For I was kind and beloved during my rule.
6:12But now I remember the evils I committed in Jerusalem: I took all the silver and gold vessels in it and sent to destroy the inhabitants of Judah without cause.
6:13I know that because of these things these evils have found me. Behold! I am perishing in great sorrow in a foreign land.”
6:14He summoned Philip, one of his Friends, and appointed him over his whole kingdom.
6:15He gave him the diadem, his robe, and his ring, to guide his son Antiochus and bring him up to reign.
6:16King Antiochus died there in the one hundred and forty-ninth year.
6:17Lysias learned that the king had died and appointed his son Antiochus, whom he had brought up from youth, to reign. He called his name Eupator.
6:18Those in the citadel were hemming Israel in around the holy places, continually seeking harm, and providing support to the nations.
6:19Judas determined to remove them and assembled all the people to besiege them.
6:20They gathered together and besieged it in the one hundred and fiftieth year. He made artillery platforms and siege engines.
6:21Some of them escaped from the blockade, and certain ungodly men from Israel joined them.
6:22They went to the king and said, “How long will you refrain from giving judgment and avenging our brothers?
6:23We are willing to serve your father, walk according to his words, and follow his decrees.
6:24For this reason the sons of our people besieged it and became estranged from us. Moreover, as many of us as were found were put to death, and our inheritances were plundered.
6:25They have stretched out their hand not only against us but also against all their territories.
6:26Behold! Today they have encamped against the citadel in Jerusalem to seize it. They have fortified the sanctuary and Beth-zur.
6:27Unless you act against them quickly, they will do greater things than these, and you shall not be able to restrain them.”
6:28The king became angry when he heard this. He gathered all his Friends, his army commanders, and those in charge of the reins.
6:29Mercenary forces came to him from other kingdoms and from islands of the seas.
6:30His forces numbered a hundred thousand infantry, twenty thousand cavalry, and thirty-two elephants trained for war.
6:31They came through Idumea, encamped against Beth-zur, and fought for many days, making siege engines. The defenders came out, burned them with fire, and fought courageously.
6:32Judas withdrew from the citadel and encamped at Beth-zechariah opposite the king’s camp.
6:33The king rose early in the morning and set his army moving rapidly along the road to Beth-zechariah. The forces prepared for battle and sounded the trumpets.
6:34They showed the elephants the blood of grapes and mulberries to ready them for battle.

6:35They divided the beasts among the phalanxes. Beside each elephant they stationed a thousand men armoured in chain mail, with bronze helmets on their heads, and five hundred picked cavalry were assigned to each beast.
6:36They were in position beforehand wherever the beast was; wherever it went, they went together and did not leave it.
6:37Strong, covered wooden towers were on them, secured by devices upon each beast. On each were four fighting men and its Indian driver.
6:38He stationed the remaining cavalry on either side, on the two wings of the army, threatening the enemy and shielding the phalanxes.
6:39When the sun flashed upon the golden and bronze shields, the mountains flashed from them and shone like torches of fire.
6:40One part of the king’s army spread out on the high mountains and others on the low ground. They advanced securely and in order.
6:41Everyone who heard the sound of their multitude, the march of the multitude, and the clash of weapons was shaken, for the army was exceedingly large and strong.
6:42Judas and his army drew near for battle, and six hundred men of the king’s army fell.
6:43Eleazar Avaran saw one of the beasts armoured with royal breastplates, towering above all the beasts, and thought that the king was on it.
6:44He gave himself to save his people and to gain for himself an everlasting name.
6:45He ran boldly toward it into the midst of the phalanx, killing to the right and left, and they parted before him on either side.
6:46He slipped beneath the elephant, thrust under it, and killed it. It fell to the ground on top of him, and he died there.
6:47They saw the strength of the kingdom and the onrush of the forces and withdrew from them.
6:48The men of the king’s army went up to meet them at Jerusalem, and the king encamped in Judea and against Mount Zion.
6:49He made peace with the people of Beth-zur, and they came out of the city, because they had no provisions there to sustain a siege, since it was a sabbath for the land.
6:50The king seized Beth-zur and stationed a garrison there to guard it.
6:51He encamped against the sanctuary for many days and set up artillery platforms, siege engines, fire-throwers, stone-throwers, small scorpions for shooting missiles, and slings.
6:52The defenders also made engines to oppose their engines and fought for many days.
6:53There was no food in the storage vessels, because it was the seventh year, and those who had escaped into Judea from the nations had consumed the remaining stores.
6:54Only a few men were left in the holy places, because famine prevailed over them. They scattered, each to his own place.
6:55Lysias heard that Philip, whom King Antiochus had appointed while still alive to bring up his son Antiochus to reign,
6:56had returned from Persia and Media with the forces that had gone with the king, and that he was seeking to take control of affairs.

6:57He hurried and pressed for departure, saying to the king, the commanders of the force, and the men, “We are dwindling day by day, our food is scarce, the place against which we are encamped is strong, and the affairs of the kingdom are pressing upon us.
6:58Now, therefore, let us give these men our right hands and make peace with them and with their whole nation.
6:59Let us establish their right to follow their customs as before. For it was because of their customs, which we abolished, that they became angry and did all these things.”
6:60The proposal pleased the king and the commanders. He sent to make peace with them, and they accepted.
6:61The king and the commanders swore to them, and on these terms they came out of the stronghold.
6:62The king entered Mount Zion and saw the strength of the place. He rejected the oath he had sworn and ordered the surrounding wall to be pulled down.
6:63He set out hurriedly and returned to Antioch. He found Philip in control of the city, fought against him, and seized the city by force.
7:1In the one hundred and fifty-first year, Demetrius son of Seleucus departed from Rome, came up with a few men to a coastal city, and reigned there.
7:2As he was entering the royal house of his fathers, the forces seized Antiochus and Lysias to bring them to him.
7:3The matter became known to him, and he said, “Do not show me their faces.”
7:4The forces killed them, and Demetrius sat upon the throne of his kingdom.
7:5All the lawless and ungodly men from Israel came to him. Alcimus, who wished to serve as priest, was their leader.
7:6They accused the people before the king, saying, “Judas and his brothers have destroyed all your Friends and scattered us from our land.
7:7Now, therefore, send a man whom you trust. Let him go and see all the devastation he has brought upon us and the king’s country, and let him punish them and all who help them.”
7:8The king chose Bacchides, one of the king’s Friends, who ruled Beyond the River, was great in the kingdom, and was faithful to the king.
7:9He sent him and the ungodly Alcimus, confirmed Alcimus in the priesthood, and commanded Bacchides to exact vengeance among the sons of Israel.
7:10They set out and came with a large force into the land of Judah. He sent messengers to Judas and his brothers with peaceful words, deceitfully.
7:11They paid no attention to their words, for they saw that they had come with a large force.
7:12A company of scribes gathered to Alcimus and Bacchides to seek just terms.
7:13The Hasideans were the first among the sons of Israel to seek peace from them,
7:14for they said, “A man who is a priest of Aaron’s line has come with the forces, and he will not wrong us.”
7:15He spoke peaceful words with them and swore to them, saying, “We will not seek harm for you or your friends.”
7:16They trusted him. But he seized sixty men from among them and killed them in one day, according to the word that was written:
7:17“They poured out the flesh of Thy holy ones and their blood around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them.”
7:18Fear and trembling because of them fell upon all the people, for they said, “There is no truth or justice in them; they have violated the agreement and the oath they swore.”
7:19Bacchides withdrew from Jerusalem and encamped at Beth-zaith. He sent and seized many of the men who had deserted to him and some of the people, and slaughtered them into the great pit.
7:20He placed the country under Alcimus and left a force with him to help him. Then Bacchides went to the king.
7:21Alcimus contended for the high priesthood.
7:22All who troubled their people gathered to him, took control of the land of Judah, and inflicted a great blow upon Israel.
7:23Judas saw all the evil that Alcimus and those with him had committed among the sons of Israel, beyond that of the nations.
7:24He went out throughout all the territory of Judea and exacted vengeance on the deserters. They were prevented from going out into the country.
7:25Alcimus saw that Judas and those with him had grown strong and knew that he could not stand against them. He returned to the king and brought evil accusations against them.
7:26The king sent Nicanor, one of his distinguished commanders, who hated Israel and was hostile to them, and commanded him to destroy the people.
7:27Nicanor came to Jerusalem with a large force. He sent deceitfully to Judas and his brothers with peaceful words, saying,
7:28“Let there be no battle between me and you. I will come with a few men so that I may see your faces in peace.”
7:29He came to Judas, and they greeted one another peacefully, but the enemies were ready to seize Judas.
7:30Judas learned that he had come against him deceitfully. He became wary of him and would no longer see his face.
7:31Nicanor knew that his plan had been revealed and went out to meet Judas in battle near Caphar-salama.
7:32About five hundred of Nicanor’s men fell, and they fled into the city of David.

7:33After these events Nicanor went up to Mount Zion. Some of the priests came out of the holy places, together with some elders of the people, to greet him peacefully and show him the whole burnt offering being presented for the king.
7:34He sneered at them, mocked them, defiled them, and spoke arrogantly.
7:35He swore in anger, saying, “Unless Judas and his army are handed over into my hands now, if I return safely, I will burn this house.” He went out in great anger.
7:36The priests went in and stood before the altar and the temple. They wept and said,
7:37“Thou didst choose this house for Thy name to be called upon it, to be a house of prayer and petition for Thy people.
7:38Exact vengeance upon this man and his army, and let them fall by the sword. Remember their insults, and grant them no continuance.”
7:39Nicanor went out from Jerusalem and encamped at Beth-horon, and a Syrian force met him.
7:40Judas encamped at Adasa with three thousand men. Judas prayed and said,
7:41“When the king’s men spoke blasphemously, Thine angel went out and struck a hundred and eighty-five thousand among them.
7:42In this way crush this army before us today. Let the survivors know that he has spoken wickedly against Thy holy places, and judge him according to his wickedness.”
7:43The armies joined battle on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar. Nicanor’s army was crushed, and he himself fell first in the battle.
7:44When his army saw that Nicanor had fallen, they threw down their weapons and fled.
7:45They pursued them a day’s journey from Adasa until they came to Gazera, sounding the signal trumpets behind them.
7:46People came out from all the surrounding villages of Judea and outflanked them. They turned against one another and all fell by the sword; not even one of them remained.
7:47They took the spoils and plunder, cut off Nicanor’s head and his right hand, which he had stretched out arrogantly, and brought and displayed them beside Jerusalem.
7:48The people rejoiced greatly and celebrated that day as a day of great gladness.
7:49They established that this day should be celebrated every year, on the thirteenth of Adar.
7:50The land of Judah was quiet for a few days.

8:1Judas heard the reputation of the Romans: that they were mighty in strength, that they looked favourably on all who joined them, that they established friendship with whoever approached them, and that they were mighty in strength.
8:2They recounted to him their wars, the brave deeds they were doing among the Galatians, and how they had subdued them and brought them under tribute;
8:3also what they had done in the country of Spain to gain control of the silver and gold mines there.

8:4By their counsel and perseverance they had gained control of the whole region, although it was very far from them. They had also overcome the kings who came against them from the end of the earth, crushing them and striking them a great blow; the survivors paid them tribute every year.
8:5They had crushed in battle Philip, Perseus king of the Kittians, and those who rose against them, and had subdued them.
8:6Antiochus the Great, king of Asia, had marched against them for battle with a hundred and twenty elephants, cavalry, chariots, and an exceedingly large force, but he was crushed by them.
8:7They took him alive and required him and those reigning after him to pay a great tribute, give hostages, and make a territorial settlement,
8:8including the country of India, Media, and Lydia, some of their finest regions. They took them from him and gave them to King Eumenes.
8:9They also heard that the people of Greece had resolved to come and destroy them.

8:10The Romans learned the plan and sent one general against them. They fought them, and many fell wounded; they took their wives and children captive, plundered them, subdued their land, demolished their strongholds, and enslaved them to this day.
8:11The remaining kingdoms and islands, as many as ever resisted them, they destroyed and enslaved. But with their friends and those who relied on them they maintained friendship.
8:12They subdued kings near and far, and all who heard their name feared them.
8:13Those whom they wish to help and to have as kings do reign; those whom they wish to remove, they remove. They have been greatly exalted.
8:14Yet in all these things not one of them has put on a diadem or clothed himself in purple to magnify himself by it.
8:15They made a council chamber for themselves, and every day three hundred and twenty men deliberated, continually taking counsel concerning the people so that they might be well ordered.
8:16Each year they entrust one man to rule them and govern their whole land. All obey the one, and there is no envy or rivalry among them.
8:17Judas chose Eupolemus son of John son of Accos, and Jason son of Eleazar, and sent them to Rome to establish friendship and an alliance
8:18and to remove the yoke from them, because they saw the kingdom of the Greeks enslaving Israel in servitude.
8:19They went to Rome, a very long journey, entered the council chamber, and spoke, saying,
8:20“Judas, also called Maccabeus, his brothers, and the people of the Jews have sent us to you to establish an alliance and peace with you, and to have us enrolled as your allies and friends.”
8:21The proposal pleased them.
8:22This is the copy of the letter they inscribed on bronze tablets and sent to Jerusalem to remain there with them as a memorial of peace and alliance:
8:23“May it be well with the Romans and the nation of the Jews on sea and on dry land for ever, and may sword and enemy be far from them.
8:24If war comes first upon Rome or upon any of their allies throughout their whole dominion,
8:25the nation of the Jews shall fight alongside them wholeheartedly, as circumstances prescribe for them.
8:26They shall neither give nor supply grain, weapons, money, or ships to those making war, as Rome has decided. They shall keep their obligations, receiving nothing.
8:27Likewise, if war comes first upon the nation of the Jews, the Romans shall fight alongside them with all their soul, as circumstances prescribe for them.
8:28To those acting as allies, grain, weapons, money, and ships shall not be given, as Rome has decided. They shall keep these obligations without deceit.
8:29On these terms the Romans thus established an agreement with the Jewish people.
8:30If after these terms both parties decide to add or remove anything, they shall do so by their own choice; whatever they add or remove shall be binding.
8:31Concerning the evils that King Demetrius is committing against them, we have written to him, saying, ‘Why have you made your yoke heavy upon our friends and allies, the Jews?
8:32If, therefore, they appeal against you again, we will give judgment for them and make war on you by sea and by land.’”
9:1Demetrius heard that Nicanor and his force had fallen in battle, and again sent Bacchides and Alcimus into the land of Judah, with the right wing of the army.
9:2They travelled the road to Gilgal, encamped against Mesaloth in Arbela, seized it, and destroyed many human lives.
9:3In the first month of the one hundred and fifty-second year they encamped against Jerusalem.
9:4They set out and went to Berea with twenty thousand men and two thousand cavalry.
9:5Judas was encamped at Elasa with three thousand picked men.
9:6They saw the multitude of the forces, how many they were, and became exceedingly afraid. Many slipped away from the camp, and only eight hundred men were left.
9:7Judas saw that his army had slipped away and that the battle was pressing upon him. His heart was crushed, because he had no time to gather them.
9:8He grew faint and said to those remaining, “Let us arise and go up against our adversaries, if perhaps we can fight them.”
9:9They tried to turn him back, saying, “We certainly cannot! Let us save our lives for now. We will return with our brothers and fight them, but we are few.”
9:10Judas said, “Far be it from us to do this thing and flee from them! If our time has drawn near, let us die courageously for our brothers and leave no charge against our glory.”

9:11The force moved out of the camp and took position to meet them. The cavalry was divided into two parts; the slingers and archers went ahead of the force, and all the foremost fighters were mighty men. Bacchides was on the right wing.
9:12The phalanx approached from both sides, and they sounded the trumpets. Judas’s men also sounded their trumpets.
9:13The earth was shaken by the sound of the armies, and battle was joined from morning until evening.
9:14Judas saw that Bacchides and the strongest part of the army were on the right. All who were courageous in heart gathered to him,
9:15and the right wing was crushed by them. He pursued them as far as Mount Azotus.
9:16Those on the left wing saw that the right wing had been crushed, and turned to follow on the heels of Judas and those with him from behind.
9:17The battle grew heavy, and many fell wounded on both sides.
9:18Judas fell, and the rest fled.
9:19Jonathan and Simon took up Judas their brother and buried him in the tomb of his fathers in Modein.
9:20They wept for him, and all Israel lamented him with a great lament. They mourned for many days and said,
9:21“How has the mighty one fallen, the saviour of Israel!”
9:22The rest of the deeds of Judas, his battles, the brave deeds he performed, and his greatness were not written down, for they were exceedingly many.
9:23After the death of Judas, the lawless emerged throughout all Israel’s territory, and all who practiced injustice rose up.
9:24In those days an exceedingly great famine occurred, and the country went over to their side.
9:25Bacchides chose the ungodly men and appointed them masters of the country.
9:26They sought out and searched for Judas’s friends and brought them to Bacchides, who punished and mocked them.
9:27Great distress came upon Israel, such as had not occurred since the day a prophet was no longer seen among them.
9:28All Judas’s friends gathered and said to Jonathan,
9:29“Since your brother Judas died, there is no man like him to go out and come in against our enemies, Bacchides, and those hostile to our nation.
9:30Now, therefore, today we have chosen you to be our ruler and leader in his place, to fight our war.”
9:31Jonathan accepted the leadership at that time and arose in place of Judas his brother.
9:32Bacchides learned of it and sought to kill him.
9:33Jonathan, Simon his brother, and all who were with him learned of it and fled into the wilderness of Tekoa. They encamped by the water of the pool of Asphar.
9:34Bacchides learned of it on the sabbath day, and he and his whole army came beyond the Jordan.
9:35Jonathan sent his brother, a leader of the company, and appealed to his friends the Nabateans to allow their many belongings to be deposited with them.
9:36The sons of Jambri from Medaba came out, seized John and everything he had, and went away with it.

9:37After these events they reported to Jonathan and Simon his brother, “The sons of Jambri are holding a great wedding and bringing the bride from Nadabath, the daughter of one of the great nobles of Canaan, with a great escort.”
9:38They remembered the blood of John their brother, went up, and hid under the cover of the mountain.
9:39They raised their eyes and saw a commotion and much baggage. The bridegroom, his friends, and his brothers came out to meet them with tambourines, musicians, and many weapons.
9:40They rose against them from the ambush and killed them. Many fell wounded, and the survivors fled into the mountain. They took all their spoils.
9:41The wedding was turned into mourning, and the sound of their musicians into lamentation.
9:42They exacted vengeance for their brother’s blood and returned to the marsh of the Jordan.
9:43Bacchides heard and came on the sabbath day to the banks of the Jordan with a large force.
9:44Jonathan said to his men, “Come, let us arise and fight for our lives, for today is not like yesterday or the day before.
9:45Behold! Battle is before us and behind us, the water of the Jordan is on either side, and there are marsh and thicket. There is nowhere to turn aside.
9:46Now, therefore, cry out to Heaven so that you may be rescued from the hand of our enemies.”
9:47The battle was joined. Jonathan stretched out his hand to strike Bacchides, but he withdrew backward from him.
9:48Jonathan and those with him leaped into the Jordan and swam across. The enemy did not cross the Jordan after them.
9:49About a thousand of Bacchides’s men fell that day.
9:50He returned to Jerusalem. They built fortified cities in Judea: the stronghold at Jericho, Emmaus, Beth-horon, Bethel, Thamnatha-Pharathon, and Tephon, with high walls, gates, and bars.
9:51He placed garrisons in them to act against Israel.
9:52He fortified the city of Beth-zur, Gazara, and the citadel, and placed forces and stores of food in them.
9:53He took the sons of the leaders of the country as hostages and placed them under guard in the citadel at Jerusalem.
9:54In the second month of the one hundred and fifty-third year, Alcimus ordered the wall of the inner court of the holy places to be demolished. He began tearing down the works of the prophets.
9:55At that time Alcimus was struck, and his work was obstructed. His mouth was stopped, and he was paralyzed, unable to speak another word or give orders concerning his household.
9:56Alcimus died at that time in great torment.
9:57Bacchides saw that Alcimus had died and returned to the king. The land of Judah was quiet for two years.
9:58All the lawless took counsel, saying, “Behold! Jonathan and his men are living quietly and confidently. Let us now bring up Bacchides, and he will seize them all in one night.”
9:59They went and conferred with him.
9:60He set out to come with a large force and secretly sent letters to all his allies in Judea to seize Jonathan and those with him. But they could not, because their plan had become known.
9:61Jonathan’s men seized about fifty men from the country who were ringleaders of the evil and killed them.
9:62Jonathan, Simon, and those with him withdrew to Beth-basi in the wilderness. He rebuilt its demolished parts, and they strengthened it.
9:63Bacchides learned of it, gathered his whole multitude, and gave orders to those from Judea.
9:64He came, encamped against Beth-basi, attacked it for many days, and made siege engines.
9:65Jonathan left Simon his brother in the city, went out into the country, and came with a small number.
9:66He struck Odomera, his brothers, and the sons of Phasiron in their encampment. They began striking and advancing with their forces.
9:67Simon and those with him came out of the city and burned the siege engines.
9:68They fought Bacchides, and he was crushed by them. They pressed him greatly, for his plan and his expedition had come to nothing.
9:69He became furious with the lawless men who had advised him to come into the country, killed many of them, and resolved to depart to his own land.
9:70Jonathan learned of it and sent envoys to him to arrange peace with him and to return the captives to them.
9:71He accepted and acted according to his words, and swore to him that he would not seek his harm all the days of his life.
9:72He returned to him the captives he had previously taken from the land of Judah. He turned and went away to his own land and did not come again into their territory.
9:73The sword ceased from Israel. Jonathan settled in Michmash, began to judge the people, and removed the ungodly from Israel.
10:1In the one hundred and sixtieth year Alexander Epiphanes, son of Antiochus, came up and seized Ptolemais. They received him, and he reigned there.
10:2King Demetrius heard of it, gathered very large forces, and went out to meet him in battle.
10:3Demetrius sent letters to Jonathan with peaceful words, intending to exalt him.
10:4For he said, “Let us be first to make peace with them before he makes an agreement with Alexander against us.
10:5He will remember all the evils we have committed against him, his brothers, and the nation.”
10:6He gave him authority to gather forces, prepare weapons, and be his ally. He ordered that the hostages in the citadel be handed over to him.
10:7Jonathan came to Jerusalem and read the letters in the hearing of all the people and those in the citadel.
10:8They were greatly afraid when they heard that the king had given him authority to gather a force.
10:9Those in the citadel handed over the hostages to Jonathan, and he returned them to their parents.
10:10Jonathan settled in Jerusalem and began rebuilding and renewing the city.
10:11He told the workers to build the walls and the enclosure around Mount Zion with four-foot stones for fortification, and they did so.
10:12The foreigners in the strongholds that Bacchides had built fled.
10:13Each abandoned his place and went to his own land.
10:14Only at Beth-zur did some who had abandoned the law and the decrees remain, for it was a place of refuge.
10:15King Alexander heard all the promises Demetrius had sent Jonathan. They recounted to him the battles and brave deeds that he and his brothers had performed, and the hardships they had endured.
10:16He said, “Could we find another man like this? Now we will make him our friend and ally.”
10:17He wrote letters and sent them to him in these words:
10:18“King Alexander to his brother Jonathan, greetings.
10:19We have heard concerning you, that you are a man mighty in strength and suitable to be our friend.

10:20Now, therefore, today we have appointed you high priest of your nation and to be called the king’s Friend”—and he sent him a purple robe and a golden crown—“to be concerned for our interests and maintain friendship with us.”
10:21Jonathan put on the holy robe in the seventh month of the one hundred and sixtieth year, at the Festival of Booths. He gathered forces and prepared many weapons.
10:22Demetrius heard these things and was grieved. He said,
10:23“What have we done, that Alexander has anticipated us in securing friendship with the Jews for support?
10:24I too will write them words of encouragement, honour, and gifts, so that they may be with me to help.”
10:25He sent to them in these words: “King Demetrius to the nation of the Jews, greetings.
10:26We have heard that you have kept your agreements with us, remained in our friendship, and not joined our enemies, and we rejoiced.
10:27Now continue to keep faith with us, and we will repay you with good things for what you do with us.
10:28We will grant you many remissions and give you gifts.
10:29Now I release you and exempt all the Jews from tribute, the salt charge, and crown payments.

10:30I relinquish from today onward the right to receive the third of the grain crop and the half of the fruit of the trees that fall to me, from the land of Judah and the three districts added to it from Samaria and Galilee, from this day and for all time.
10:31Let Jerusalem and its territory be holy and exempt, free of tithes and dues.
10:32I also relinquish authority over the citadel in Jerusalem and give it to the high priest, so that he may appoint in it men of his own choosing to guard it.
10:33Every Jewish person taken captive from the land of Judah into any part of my kingdom I release freely, without payment. Let all remit their taxes, including those upon their livestock.
10:34Let all festivals, sabbaths, new moons, and appointed days, and the three days before a festival and the three after it, all be days of exemption and release for all Jews in my kingdom.
10:35No one shall have authority to exact payment from or trouble any of them concerning any matter.
10:36Let up to thirty thousand men of the Jews be enrolled in the king’s forces, and let allowances be given to them, as is proper for all the king’s forces.

10:37Some of them shall be stationed in the king’s great strongholds, and some shall be appointed to positions of trust in the kingdom. Their supervisors and commanders shall be from among them, and they shall follow their own laws, as the king has also decreed in the land of Judah.
10:38Let the three districts added to Judea from the region of Samaria be attached to Judea, so that they may be reckoned under one authority and obey no other authority except the high priest.
10:39I have given Ptolemais and the territory belonging to it as a gift to the holy places in Jerusalem, for the expenses proper to the holy places.
10:40I myself give every year fifteen thousand shekels of silver from the king’s accounts, from the appropriate places.
10:41All the excess that they did not pay from the revenues as in former years they shall from now on give for the works of the house.

10:42Besides these, the five thousand shekels of silver that they used to take from the revenues of the holy place from its account each year are also remitted, because they belong to the priests who minister.
10:43All who flee to the temple in Jerusalem and anywhere within its precincts, owing royal dues or any other obligation, shall be released, together with all they possess in my kingdom.
10:44The cost of rebuilding and renewing the works of the holy places shall be given from the king’s account.
10:45The cost of rebuilding Jerusalem’s walls and fortifying it all around shall be given from the king’s account, and likewise for rebuilding walls in Judea.”
10:46When Jonathan and the people heard these words, they neither believed nor accepted them, because they remembered the great evil he had committed in Israel and how severely he had oppressed them.
10:47They favoured Alexander, because he had been the first to speak peaceful words to them, and they remained his allies all his days.
10:48King Alexander gathered great forces and encamped opposite Demetrius.
10:49The two kings joined battle. Demetrius’s army fled; Alexander pursued him and prevailed against them.
10:50He pressed the battle fiercely until the sun went down, and Demetrius fell that day.
10:51Alexander sent envoys to Ptolemy king of Egypt in these words:
10:52“I have returned to my kingdom, sat upon the throne of my fathers, and taken control of the government. I have crushed Demetrius and gained control of our country.
10:53I joined battle with him, and he and his army were crushed by us. We have sat upon the throne of his kingdom.
10:54Now let us establish friendship with one another. Give me your daughter as wife, and I will become your son-in-law and give you and her gifts worthy of you.”
10:55King Ptolemy answered, saying, “The day you returned to the land of your fathers and sat upon the throne of their kingdom was a good day.
10:56Now I will do for you what you have written. But meet me at Ptolemais, so that we may see one another, and I will form a marriage alliance with you as you have said.”
10:57Ptolemy left Egypt with Cleopatra his daughter and came to Ptolemais in the one hundred and sixty-second year.
10:58King Alexander met him, and he gave him Cleopatra his daughter in marriage and celebrated her wedding at Ptolemais with great glory, as kings do.
10:59King Alexander wrote to Jonathan to come and meet him.
10:60He went in honour to Ptolemais and met the two kings. He gave them and their Friends silver, gold, and many gifts, and found favour before them.
10:61Pestilent men from Israel, lawless men, gathered against him to petition against him, but the king paid no attention to them.
10:62The king ordered them to remove Jonathan’s garments and clothe him in purple, and they did so.

10:63The king seated him with himself and said to his commanders, “Go out with him into the midst of the city and proclaim that no one may petition against him concerning any matter, and that no one may trouble him concerning any charge.”
10:64When the accusers saw his honour as proclaimed and saw him clothed in purple, they all fled.
10:65The king honoured him, enrolled him among the First Friends, and appointed him general and district governor.
10:66Jonathan returned to Jerusalem in peace and gladness.
10:67In the one hundred and sixty-fifth year, Demetrius son of Demetrius came from Crete into the land of his fathers.
10:68King Alexander heard of it, was greatly distressed, and returned to Antioch.
10:69Demetrius appointed Apollonius, who was over Coele-Syria. He gathered a great force and encamped against Jamnia, and sent to Jonathan the high priest, saying,
10:70“You alone are raising yourself against us, and because of you I have become an object of ridicule and reproach. Why are you exercising power against us in the mountains?
10:71Now, if you trust in your forces, come down to us into the plain, and let us measure ourselves against one another there, for a force from the cities is with me.
10:72Ask and learn who I am and who the others helping us are. They say, ‘There is no foothold for you before us, because your fathers were routed twice in their own land.’
10:73Now you shall not be able to stand against the cavalry and such a force in the plain, where there is neither stone nor pebble nor a place to flee.”
10:74When Jonathan heard Apollonius’s words, he was stirred in mind. He chose ten thousand men and went out from Jerusalem; Simon his brother met him to help him.
10:75He encamped against Joppa. The people of the city shut it against him, because Apollonius’s garrison was in Joppa, and they attacked it.
10:76The people of the city became afraid and opened it, and Jonathan gained control of Joppa.

10:77Apollonius heard and brought three thousand cavalry and a large force into camp. He went toward Azotus as though passing through, while drawing forward into the plain because he had many cavalry and trusted in them.
10:78Jonathan pursued him toward Azotus, and the armies joined battle.
10:79Apollonius had secretly left a thousand cavalry behind them.
10:80Jonathan realized there was an ambush behind him. They surrounded his army and hurled missiles at the people from morning until evening.
10:81But the people stood firm, as Jonathan had commanded, and their enemies’ horses grew weary.
10:82Simon drew out his force and engaged the phalanx, for the cavalry was exhausted. They were crushed by him and fled,
10:83and the cavalry scattered in the plain. They fled into Azotus and entered Beth-dagon, their idol shrine, for safety.
10:84Jonathan burned Azotus and its surrounding towns and took their spoils. He burned the temple of Dagon and those who had fled into it with fire.
10:85Those who had fallen by the sword, together with those burned, numbered about eight thousand men.
10:86Jonathan set out from there and encamped against Ascalon. The people of the city came out to meet him with great honour.
10:87Jonathan returned to Jerusalem with his men, carrying many spoils.
10:88When King Alexander heard these things, he honoured Jonathan still more.
10:89He sent him a golden clasp, as is customarily given to the king’s Kinsmen, and gave him Ekron and all its territory as an inheritance.
11:1The king of Egypt gathered many forces, like the sand beside the seashore, and many ships. He sought to gain control of Alexander’s kingdom by deceit and add it to his own kingdom.
11:2He went out to Syria with peaceful words. The people of the cities opened to him and met him, because King Alexander had commanded them to meet him, since he was his father-in-law.
11:3As Ptolemy entered the cities, he stationed forces as a garrison in each city.

11:4When they approached Azotus, they showed him the burned temple of Dagon, Azotus and its surrounding towns demolished, the bodies thrown out, and those whom Jonathan had burned in the war. They had piled them in heaps along his route.
11:5They recounted to the king what Jonathan had done, to bring blame upon him. But the king remained silent.
11:6Jonathan met the king at Joppa with honour. They greeted one another and lodged there.
11:7Jonathan accompanied the king as far as the river called Eleutherus, then returned to Jerusalem.
11:8King Ptolemy gained control of the coastal cities as far as Seleucia by the sea, and devised evil plans concerning Alexander.
11:9He sent envoys to King Demetrius, saying, “Come, let us make a covenant with one another, and I will give you my daughter whom Alexander had, and you shall reign over your father’s kingdom.
11:10For I regret giving him my daughter, because he sought to kill me.”
11:11He accused him because he desired his kingdom.
11:12He took his daughter away from him, gave her to Demetrius, and became estranged from Alexander; their hostility became evident.
11:13Ptolemy entered Antioch and put on the diadem of Asia. He placed two diadems on his head, that of Egypt and that of Asia.
11:14King Alexander was in Cilicia at that time, because the people of those places were in revolt.
11:15Alexander heard and came against him in battle. Ptolemy led out his forces, met him with a strong force, and routed him.
11:16Alexander fled into Arabia to find shelter there, and King Ptolemy was exalted.
11:17Zabdiel the Arab cut off Alexander’s head and sent it to Ptolemy.
11:18King Ptolemy died on the third day, and his men in the strongholds were destroyed by those in the strongholds.
11:19Demetrius became king in the one hundred and sixty-seventh year.
11:20In those days Jonathan gathered the men of Judea to make war on the citadel in Jerusalem, and he made many siege engines against it.
11:21Some lawless men who hated their own nation went to the king and reported to him that Jonathan was besieging the citadel.

11:22When he heard, he became angry. Immediately on hearing it he set out and came to Ptolemais. He wrote to Jonathan to stop the siege and to come as quickly as possible to confer with him at Ptolemais.
11:23When Jonathan heard, he ordered the siege to continue, selected some elders of Israel and priests, and exposed himself to danger.
11:24He took silver, gold, clothing, and many other gifts, went to the king at Ptolemais, and found favour before him.
11:25Some lawless men from the nation were petitioning against him.
11:26The king treated him as those before him had done and exalted him before all his Friends.
11:27He confirmed him in the high priesthood and all the other honours he had held before, and made him rank among the First Friends.
11:28Jonathan asked the king to make Judea, the three districts, and Samaria free from tribute, and promised him three hundred talents.
11:29The king consented and wrote letters to Jonathan concerning all these things in the following form:
