11:30“King Demetrius to Jonathan his brother and to the nation of the Jews, greetings.
11:31We have also written to you a copy of the letter we wrote about you to Lasthenes our Kinsman, so that you may know it.
11:32‘King Demetrius to Lasthenes his father, greetings.
11:33We have judged it good to benefit the nation of the Jews, our friends who keep their obligations toward us, because of their goodwill toward us.

11:34We have confirmed to them the territory of Judea and the three districts of Aphairema, Lydda, and Rathamin, added to Judea from Samaria, with everything belonging to them, for all who sacrifice in Jerusalem, in place of the royal dues that the king formerly received from them each year from the produce of the land and the fruit trees.
11:35The other things belonging to us from now on—the tithes and dues belonging to us, the salt lakes, and the crown payments belonging to us—we grant all these to them.
11:36Not one of these provisions shall be annulled from now and for all time.
11:37Now, therefore, take care to make a copy of these things. Let it be given to Jonathan and placed on the holy mountain in a conspicuous place.’”

11:38King Demetrius saw that the land was quiet before him and that nothing resisted him. He dismissed all his forces, each to his own place, except the foreign forces he had recruited from the islands of the nations. All the forces inherited from his fathers became hostile to him.
11:39Tryphon had formerly been one of Alexander’s men. He saw that all the forces were grumbling against Demetrius and went to Imalcue the Arab, who was bringing up Alexander’s young son Antiochus.

11:40He stayed with him, urging him to hand the boy over so that he might reign in his father’s place. He reported everything Demetrius had done and the hostility his forces felt toward him, and remained there many days.
11:41Jonathan sent to King Demetrius, asking him to remove the men of the citadel from Jerusalem and those in the strongholds, because they were fighting Israel.
11:42Demetrius sent to Jonathan, saying, “I will do not only these things for you and your nation, but I will greatly honour you and your nation if I find an opportunity.
11:43Now, therefore, you will do well to send me men who will fight alongside me, because all my forces have revolted.”
11:44Jonathan sent three thousand men mighty in strength to him at Antioch. They came to the king, and the king rejoiced at their arrival.
11:45The people of the city gathered in its midst, about a hundred and twenty thousand men, intending to kill the king.
11:46The king fled into the palace. The people of the city seized its passageways and began fighting.
11:47The king called the Jews to help. They all gathered to him together, spread through the city, and killed about a hundred thousand that day.
11:48They burned the city, took many spoils that day, and saved the king.
11:49The people of the city saw that the Jews controlled the city as they wished. They lost courage and cried to the king with a plea, saying,
11:50“Give us your right hand, and let the Jews stop fighting us and the city.”
11:51They threw down their weapons and made peace. The Jews were honoured before the king and before everyone in his kingdom, and returned to Jerusalem with many spoils.
11:52King Demetrius sat upon the throne of his kingdom, and the land was quiet before him.
11:53He proved false in everything he had said, became estranged from Jonathan, did not repay the goodwill shown to him, and oppressed him greatly.
11:54After this Tryphon returned, and with him Antiochus, a young boy. Antiochus became king and put on a diadem.
11:55All the forces Demetrius had dismissed gathered to him. They fought Demetrius, and he fled and was routed.
11:56Tryphon took the elephants and gained control of Antioch.
11:57The young Antiochus wrote to Jonathan, saying, “I confirm you in the high priesthood, appoint you over the four districts, and make you one of the king’s Friends.”
11:58He sent him gold vessels and a table service, and granted him authority to drink from gold vessels, wear purple, and have a golden clasp.
11:59He appointed Simon his brother general from the Ladder of Tyre to the borders of Egypt.
11:60Jonathan went out and travelled through Beyond the River and its cities. All the Syrian forces gathered to him as allies. He came to Ascalon, and the people of the city met him with honour.
11:61He went from there to Gaza, but the people of Gaza shut him out. He besieged it, burned its surrounding towns with fire, and plundered them.
11:62The people of Gaza appealed to Jonathan. He gave them his right hand, took their rulers’ sons as hostages, and sent them to Jerusalem. He passed through the country as far as Damascus.
11:63Jonathan heard that Demetrius’s commanders had arrived at Kedesh in Galilee with a large force, intending to remove him from his office.
11:64He went to meet them, leaving Simon his brother in the country.
11:65Simon encamped against Beth-zur, attacked it for many days, and blockaded it.
11:66They asked him to receive a pledge of peace, and he gave it to them. He expelled them from there, seized the city, and placed a garrison over it.
11:67Jonathan and his army encamped by the water of Gennesar. Early in the morning they went to the plain of Hazor.
11:68The army of foreigners met him in the plain, having sent out an ambush against him in the mountains, while they themselves met him from the front.
11:69The men in ambush rose from their positions and joined battle.
11:70All Jonathan’s men fled. Not one remained except Mattathias son of Absalom and Judas son of Chalphi, commanders of the army’s forces.
11:71Jonathan tore his garments, put earth on his head, and prayed.
11:72He turned back against them in battle and routed them, and they fled.
11:73Those who had fled from him saw it and returned to him. They pursued with him as far as Kedesh, to their camp, and encamped there.
11:74About three thousand men of the foreigners fell that day. Jonathan returned to Jerusalem.
12:1Jonathan saw that circumstances favoured him. He chose men and sent them to Rome to establish and renew their friendship.
12:2He also sent letters to the Spartans and other places for the same purpose.
12:3They went to Rome, entered the council chamber, and said, “Jonathan the high priest and the nation of the Jews have sent us to renew their friendship and alliance as before.”
12:4They gave them letters to the authorities in each place so that they might escort them peacefully to the land of Judah.
12:5This is the copy of the letters Jonathan wrote to the Spartans:
12:6“Jonathan the high priest, the council of elders of the nation, the priests, and the rest of the Jewish people, to the Spartans their brothers, greetings.
12:7In former times letters were sent to Onias the high priest from Areus, who reigned among you, stating that you are our brothers, as the copy below shows.
12:8Onias received the envoy with honour and accepted the letters, in which alliance and friendship were declared.
12:9Although we have no need of these things, since we have as encouragement the holy books that are in our hands,
12:10we have undertaken to send to renew brotherhood and friendship with you, so that we may not become estranged from you. For many seasons have passed since you sent to us.

12:11We therefore remember you continually at every season, at the festivals and the other appointed days, in the sacrifices we offer and in our prayers, as it is right and fitting to remember brothers.
12:12We rejoice in your glory.
12:13But many afflictions and many wars have surrounded us, and the kings around us have made war on us.
12:14We did not wish to trouble you or our other allies and friends in these wars,
12:15for we have help from Heaven helping us; we were rescued from our enemies, and our enemies were humbled.
12:16We have therefore chosen Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason and sent them to the Romans to renew the former friendship and alliance with them.
12:17We have also commanded them to go to you, greet you, and deliver our letters concerning the renewal of our brotherhood.
12:18Now you will do well to answer us concerning these matters.”
12:19This is the copy of the letters they sent to Onias:
12:20“Areus king of the Spartans to Onias the great priest, greetings.
12:21It has been found in a writing concerning the Spartans and Jews that they are brothers and are of the lineage of Abraham.
12:22Now that we have learned these things, you will do well to write to us concerning your welfare.
12:23We in turn write to you: your livestock and your property are ours, and ours are yours. We therefore command that they report to you accordingly.”
12:24Jonathan heard that Demetrius’s commanders had returned with a force larger than before to fight him.
12:25He set out from Jerusalem and met them in the region of Hamath, for he gave them no opportunity to enter his country.
12:26He sent spies into their camp. They returned and reported to him that they were arranging to fall upon them that night.
12:27When the sun went down, Jonathan commanded his men to keep watch and remain under arms, ready for battle all night. He posted sentries around the camp.
12:28The adversaries heard that Jonathan and his men were ready for battle. They were afraid and their hearts trembled, and they kindled fires in their camp.
12:29Jonathan and his men did not know until morning, for they could see the lights burning.
12:30Jonathan pursued them but did not overtake them, because they had crossed the Eleutherus River.
12:31Jonathan turned aside against the Arabs called Zabadeans, struck them, and took their spoils.
12:32He set out, came to Damascus, and passed through the whole region.
12:33Simon went out and travelled as far as Ascalon and the nearby strongholds. He turned aside to Joppa and seized it,
12:34for he had heard that they wished to hand over the stronghold to Demetrius’s men. He placed a garrison there to guard it.
12:35Jonathan returned, assembled the elders of the people, and deliberated with them about building strongholds in Judea

12:36and raising Jerusalem’s walls higher, and building a great barrier between the citadel and the city to separate it from the city, so that it might stand alone and its people could neither buy nor sell.
12:37They gathered to rebuild the city. Part of the wall by the stream on the east had fallen, and he repaired the section called Chaphenatha.
12:38Simon rebuilt Adida in the Shephelah, fortified it, and fitted it with doors and bars.
12:39Tryphon sought to reign over Asia, put on the diadem, and stretch out his hand against King Antiochus.
12:40He feared that Jonathan might not permit him and might fight against him. He sought to seize and destroy him, and set out and came to Beth-shan.
12:41Jonathan went out to meet him with forty thousand picked men for battle, and came to Beth-shan.
12:42Tryphon saw that he had come with a large force and feared to stretch out his hands against him.
12:43He received him with honour, introduced him to all his Friends, gave him gifts, and commanded his Friends and forces to obey him as they obeyed himself.
12:44He said to Jonathan, “Why have you wearied all these people when no war threatens us?

12:45Now send them to their homes, choose a few men to remain with you, and come with me to Ptolemais. I will hand it over to you, along with the other strongholds, the remaining forces, and all who are in charge of affairs. Then I will turn and go away, for this is why I have come.”
12:46Jonathan trusted him and did as he said. He sent away the forces, and they departed to the land of Judah.
12:47He kept three thousand men with himself, of whom he left two thousand in Galilee, while a thousand accompanied him.
12:48When Jonathan entered Ptolemais, the people of Ptolemais shut the gates and seized him. They killed with the sword everyone who had entered with him.
12:49Tryphon sent forces and cavalry into Galilee and the great plain to destroy all Jonathan’s men.
12:50They learned that he had been captured and had perished, along with those with him. They encouraged one another and marched in close formation, ready for battle.
12:51Their pursuers saw that they were fighting for their lives and turned back.
12:52They all came safely into the land of Judah, mourned Jonathan and those with him, and were exceedingly afraid. All Israel mourned with great mourning.
12:53All the nations around them sought to crush them, for they said, “They have no ruler or helper. Now let us fight them and remove their memory from among humankind.”
13:1Simon heard that Tryphon had gathered a large force to enter the land of Judah and crush it.
13:2He saw that the people were trembling and terrified. He went up to Jerusalem and gathered the people.
13:3He encouraged them and said, “You yourselves know all that I, my brothers, and my father’s house have done for the laws and the holy places, and the battles and hardships we have seen.
13:4For this cause all my brothers have perished for Israel, and I alone am left.
13:5Now far be it from me to spare my life in any time of distress, for I am no better than my brothers.
13:6I will avenge my nation, the holy places, your wives, and your children, for all the nations have gathered to crush us out of hatred.”
13:7The spirit of the people was rekindled as soon as they heard these words.
13:8They answered in a loud voice, saying, “You are our leader in place of Judas and Jonathan your brother.
13:9Fight our war, and we will do everything you tell us.”
13:10He gathered all the warriors, hastened to complete Jerusalem’s walls, and fortified it all around.
13:11He sent Jonathan son of Absalom and a sufficient force with him to Joppa. He expelled those who were in it and remained there.
13:12Tryphon set out from Ptolemais with a large force to enter the land of Judah, with Jonathan under guard.
13:13Simon encamped at Adida facing the plain.
13:14Tryphon learned that Simon had arisen in place of Jonathan his brother and was about to join battle with him. He sent envoys to him, saying,
13:15“We are holding Jonathan your brother because of money he owed to the royal treasury for the offices he held.
13:16Now send a hundred talents of silver and two of his sons as hostages, so that he will not revolt against us when released, and we will release him.”
13:17Simon knew that they were speaking deceitfully to him, yet sent to fetch the money and the children, lest he incur great hostility among the people
13:18if they said, “Because I did not send him the money and the children, he perished.”
13:19He sent the children and the hundred talents, but Tryphon proved false and did not release Jonathan.
13:20After this Tryphon came to invade the country and crush it. They went around by the road to Adora. Simon and his army moved opposite him wherever he went.
13:21Those in the citadel sent envoys to Tryphon, urging him to come to them through the wilderness and send them food.
13:22Tryphon prepared all his cavalry to go, but that night there was exceedingly heavy snow, and he did not go because of the snow. He set out and came to Gilead.
13:23When he approached Bascama, he killed Jonathan, and Jonathan was buried there.
13:24Tryphon turned and went away to his own land.
13:25Simon sent and took the bones of Jonathan his brother and buried him in Modein, the city of his fathers.
13:26All Israel lamented him with a great lament and mourned him for many days.
13:27Simon built over the tomb of his father and brothers and raised it high to be seen, with dressed stone at the back and front.
13:28He erected seven pyramids, one opposite another, for his father, his mother, and his four brothers.

13:29For these he made elaborate structures, setting great columns around them. On the columns he made full suits of armour for an everlasting name, and beside the armour he carved ships, to be seen by all who sailed the sea.
13:30This is the tomb he made in Modein, remaining to this day.
13:31Tryphon dealt deceitfully with the young King Antiochus and killed him.
13:32He reigned in his place, put on the diadem of Asia, and inflicted a great blow upon the land.
13:33Simon rebuilt Judea’s strongholds, enclosed them with high towers and great walls, gates, and bars, and placed food in the strongholds.
13:34Simon chose men and sent them to King Demetrius to secure remission for the country, because all Tryphon’s acts were plunder.
13:35King Demetrius sent to him in these words, replying with a letter of this form:
13:36“King Demetrius to Simon, high priest and Friend of kings, and to the elders and nation of the Jews, greetings.
13:37We have received the golden crown and the palm branch that you sent. We are ready to make a great peace with you and to write to the officials to grant you the remissions.
13:38Everything we have established with you stands, and the strongholds you have built shall be yours.
13:39We remit offences of ignorance and sins up to this day, and the crown payment you owed. If any other levy was collected in Jerusalem, let it be collected no longer.
13:40If any of you are suitable to be enrolled among those around us, let them be enrolled, and let there be peace between us.”
13:41In the one hundred and seventieth year, the yoke of the nations was removed from Israel.
13:42The people began to write in their documents and contracts, “In the first year of Simon, great high priest, general, and leader of the Jews.”
13:43In those days he encamped against Gazara, surrounded it with camps, made a siege tower, brought it against the city, struck one tower, and took it.
13:44Those in the siege tower leaped into the city, and a great commotion arose in the city.
13:45The people of the city, with their wives and children, went up onto the wall with torn garments and cried in a loud voice, asking Simon to give them his right hand.
13:46They said, “Do not deal with us according to our wickedness, but according to your mercy.”
13:47Simon came to terms with them and did not fight them. He expelled them from the city and cleansed the houses in which the idols had been. Then he entered it, singing hymns and blessings.
13:48He removed every uncleanness from it, settled in it men who would carry out the law, further fortified it, and built himself a dwelling in it.
13:49Those in the citadel in Jerusalem were prevented from going out and coming into the country to buy and sell. They became exceedingly hungry, and many of them perished from famine.
13:50They cried to Simon to receive a pledge of peace, and he gave it to them. He expelled them from there and cleansed the citadel from its defilements.

13:51They entered it on the twenty-third day of the second month in the one hundred and seventy-first year, with praise and palm branches, with lyres, cymbals, harps, hymns, and songs, because a great enemy had been crushed out of Israel.
13:52He established that this day should be celebrated every year with gladness. He further fortified the temple mountain beside the citadel, and he and his men lived there.
13:53Simon saw that his son John was a grown man, and appointed him commander of all the forces. He lived in Gazara.
14:1In the one hundred and seventy-second year, King Demetrius gathered his forces and went to Media to obtain help for himself so that he might fight Tryphon.
14:2Arsaces king of Persia and Media heard that Demetrius had entered his territory, and sent one of his commanders to seize him alive.
14:3He went, struck Demetrius’s army, seized him, and brought him to Arsaces, who put him under guard.
14:4The land of Judah was quiet all the days of Simon. He sought good things for his nation, and his authority and glory pleased them all his days.
14:5Among all his glorious deeds he took Joppa as a harbour and made an entrance to the islands of the sea.
14:6He enlarged the borders of his nation and gained control of the country.
14:7He gathered many who had been captive and gained control of Gazara, Beth-zur, and the citadel. He removed its uncleannesses, and there was no one to oppose him.
14:9Elders sat in the squares, all conversing about good things; the young men clothed themselves in splendour and garments of war.
14:10He supplied food to the cities and equipped them with means of defence, until the fame of his glory reached the end of the earth.

14:11He made peace upon the land,
and Israel rejoiced with great gladness.

14:12Each sat beneath his vine and his fig tree,
and none made them afraid.
14:13Those who fought them ceased from the land, and the kings were crushed in those days.
14:14He strengthened all the lowly of his people. He sought out the law and removed every lawless and wicked person.
14:15He glorified the holy places and multiplied the vessels of the holy places.
14:16It was heard in Rome, and as far as Sparta, that Jonathan had died, and they were greatly grieved.
14:17When they heard that Simon his brother had become high priest in his place and was in control of the country and its cities,
14:18they wrote to him on bronze tablets to renew with him the friendship and alliance they had established with Judas and Jonathan his brothers.
14:19The letters were read before the assembly in Jerusalem.

14:20This is the copy of the letters the Spartans sent: “The rulers of the Spartans and the city to Simon the great priest, the elders, the priests, and the rest of the Jewish people, their brothers, greetings.
14:21The envoys sent to our people reported to us concerning your glory and honour, and we rejoiced at their arrival.
14:22We entered what they said in the resolutions of the people as follows: ‘Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason, envoys of the Jews, came to us to renew friendship with us.

14:23The people resolved to receive the men with honour and to place a copy of their words in the designated public records, so that the Spartan people might have a memorial.’” They wrote a copy of these things to Simon the high priest.
14:24After this Simon sent Numenius to Rome carrying a great golden shield weighing a thousand minas to establish the alliance with them.
14:25When the people heard these things, they said, “What thanks shall we return to Simon and his sons?

14:26For he, his brothers, and his father’s house stood firm, fought off Israel’s enemies, and established freedom for Israel.” They inscribed it on bronze tablets and placed them on pillars on Mount Zion.
14:27This is the copy of the inscription: “On the eighteenth of Elul, in the one hundred and seventy-second year, which is the third year under Simon the great high priest, in Asaramel,
14:28in a great assembly of priests, people, rulers of the nation, and elders of the country, a declaration was made to us:

14:29‘Since wars have often occurred in the country, Simon son of Mattathias, a priest of the sons of Joarib, and his brothers exposed themselves to danger and resisted their nation’s adversaries, so that their holy places and the law might stand. They honoured their nation with great glory.
14:30Jonathan gathered their nation, became their high priest, and was gathered to his people.
14:31Their enemies wished to invade their country and stretch out their hands against their holy places.
14:32Then Simon resisted and fought for his nation. He spent much of his own money, supplied the men of his nation’s force with weapons, and gave them pay.
14:33He fortified the cities of Judea and Beth-zur on Judea’s border, where the enemies’ weapons had formerly been, and stationed Jewish men there as a garrison.
14:34He fortified Joppa by the sea and Gazara on the borders of Azotus, where the enemies had formerly lived. He settled Jews there and provided everything necessary for their restoration.

14:35The people saw Simon’s faithfulness and the glory he had resolved to bring to his nation. They made him their leader and high priest because he had done all these things, because of the righteousness and faithfulness he maintained toward his nation, and because he sought in every way to exalt his people.

14:36In his days it prospered in his hands to remove the nations from their country, including those in the city of David at Jerusalem who had made themselves a citadel. From it they used to go out and defile the surroundings of the holy places, inflicting a great blow upon purity.
14:37He settled Jewish men in it, fortified it for the security of the country and city, and raised Jerusalem’s walls.
14:38King Demetrius accordingly confirmed him in the high priesthood,
14:39made him one of his Friends, and honoured him with great glory.
14:40For he had heard that the Jews had been addressed by the Romans as friends, allies, and brothers, and that they had received Simon’s envoys with honour;
14:41and that the Jews and priests had agreed that Simon should be their leader and high priest for ever, until a faithful prophet should arise;
14:42that he should be their general, and take care of the holy places, appointing through his authority those in charge of their works, the country, the weapons, and the strongholds;
14:43that he should take care of the holy places, be obeyed by everyone, have all documents in the country written in his name, and wear purple and gold ornaments;

14:44and that no one among the people or priests should have authority to annul any of these things, contradict what he should say, convene a gathering in the country without him, wear purple, or fasten on a golden clasp.
14:45Whoever acts contrary to these provisions or annuls any of them shall be liable.’
14:46All the people agreed to establish Simon to act according to these terms.
14:47Simon accepted and agreed to serve as high priest, to be general and ethnarch of the Jews and priests, and to preside over them all.
14:48They directed that this inscription be placed on bronze tablets and that these be set up within the enclosure of the holy places in a conspicuous place,
14:49and that copies be placed in the treasury so that Simon and his sons might possess them.”
15:1Antiochus son of King Demetrius sent letters from the islands of the sea to Simon, priest and ethnarch of the Jews, and to the whole nation.
15:2They contained the following: “King Antiochus to Simon the great priest and ethnarch, and to the nation of the Jews, greetings.
15:3Since certain pestilent men have seized the kingdom of our fathers, I wish to reclaim the kingdom and restore it as it was before. I have recruited a multitude of forces and prepared warships.
15:4I intend to land in the country to pursue those who have ruined our country and devastated many cities in my kingdom.
15:5Now, therefore, I confirm to you all the remissions that the kings before me granted you, and all the other gifts they granted you.
15:6I permit you to strike your own coinage as money for your country.
15:7Jerusalem and the holy places shall be free. All the weapons you have prepared and the strongholds you have built and hold shall remain yours.
15:8Every royal debt and all future royal dues shall be remitted to you from now and for all time.
15:9When we gain control of our kingdom, we will honour you, your nation, and the temple with great glory, so that your glory may become evident throughout the whole earth.”
15:10In the one hundred and seventy-fourth year Antiochus went out into the land of his fathers. All the forces joined him, so that only a few remained with Tryphon.
15:11Antiochus pursued him, and he fled to Dora by the sea,
15:12for he knew that evils had gathered against him and that the forces had abandoned him.
15:13Antiochus encamped against Dora, with a hundred and twenty thousand warriors and eight thousand cavalry.
15:14He surrounded the city, and the ships joined the attack from the sea. He pressed the city from land and sea and allowed no one to go out or come in.
15:15Numenius and his companions came from Rome carrying letters to the kings and countries, in which the following was written:
15:16“Lucius, consul of the Romans, to King Ptolemy, greetings.
15:17The envoys of the Jews, our friends and allies, came to us to renew the friendship and alliance established from the beginning, sent by Simon the high priest and the Jewish people.
15:18They brought a golden shield of a thousand minas.

15:19We therefore resolved to write to the kings and countries that they should not seek their harm or make war on them, their cities, or their country, and should not ally themselves with those making war against them.
15:20We decided to accept the shield from them.
15:21If, therefore, any pestilent men have escaped from their country to you, hand them over to Simon the high priest, so that he may punish them according to their law.”
15:22He wrote the same things to King Demetrius, Attalus, Ariarathes, and Arsaces,

15:23and to all the countries: to Sampsame, the Spartans, Delos, Myndos, Sicyon, Caria, Samos, Pamphylia, Lycia, Halicarnassus, Rhodes, Phaselis, Cos, Side, Aradus, Gortyna, Cnidus, Cyprus, and Cyrene.
15:24They wrote a copy of these things to Simon the high priest.
15:25On the second day King Antiochus encamped against Dora, continually bringing his forces against it, making siege engines, and blocking Tryphon from going out or coming in.
15:26Simon sent him two thousand picked men to fight alongside him, along with silver, gold, and ample equipment.
15:27He would not receive them, but annulled everything he had previously agreed with Simon and became estranged from him.
15:28He sent Athenobius, one of his Friends, to confer with him, saying, “You hold Joppa, Gazara, and the citadel in Jerusalem, cities of my kingdom.
15:29You have devastated their territories, inflicted a great blow upon the land, and gained control of many places in my kingdom.
15:30Now, therefore, hand over the cities you have seized and the tribute of the places you have taken outside the borders of Judea.

15:31Otherwise, give five hundred talents of silver in their place, and another five hundred talents for the destruction you have caused and the tribute of the cities. If not, we will come and make war on you.”
15:32Athenobius, the king’s Friend, came to Jerusalem. He saw Simon’s glory, the display of gold and silver vessels, and the large retinue, and was astonished. He reported the king’s words to him.
15:33Simon answered him, “We have neither taken foreign land nor gained control of others’ property, but the inheritance of our fathers, which our enemies unjustly seized at one time.
15:34Now that we have the opportunity, we are holding fast to the inheritance of our fathers.
15:35As for Joppa and Gazara, which you demand, these caused a great blow among the people and in our country. For these we will give a hundred talents.”
15:36He did not answer him a word, but returned angrily to the king and reported these words, Simon’s glory, and everything he had seen. The king became greatly angry.
15:37Tryphon boarded a ship and fled to Orthosia.
15:38The king appointed Cendebaeus chief commander of the coast and gave him infantry and cavalry forces.
15:39He commanded him to encamp opposite Judea, rebuild Kedron, fortify its gates, and fight the people. The king himself pursued Tryphon.
15:40Cendebaeus came to Jamnia and began provoking the people, invading Judea, taking the people captive, and killing them.
15:41He rebuilt Kedron and stationed cavalry and forces there, so that they might go out and make sorties along the roads of Judea, as the king had ordered him.
16:1John came up from Gazara and reported to Simon his father what Cendebaeus had done.

16:2Simon called his two elder sons, Judas and John, and said to them, “I, my brothers, and my father’s house have fought Israel’s wars from youth until this day, and it has prospered in our hands to rescue Israel many times.
16:3Now I have grown old, but through mercy you are mature in years. Take my place and my brother’s, go out and fight for our nation, and may help from Heaven be with you.”
16:4He chose from the country twenty thousand warriors and cavalry, and they marched against Cendebaeus and lodged in Modein.
16:5They arose in the morning and went into the plain. A large force of infantry and cavalry came to meet them, with a stream between them.
16:6He and his people encamped opposite them. He saw that the people were afraid to cross the stream, and he crossed first. The men saw him and crossed behind him.
16:7He divided the people, placing the cavalry among the infantry, for the adversaries had very many cavalry.
16:8They sounded the trumpets, and Cendebaeus and his army were routed. Many of them fell wounded, and the survivors fled into the stronghold.
16:9Then Judas, John’s brother, was wounded. John pursued them until he came to Kedron, which Cendebaeus had built.
16:10They fled into the towers in the countryside of Azotus, and he burned it with fire. About two thousand of their men fell. He returned to Judea in peace.
16:11Ptolemy son of Abubus had been appointed commander over the plain of Jericho and possessed much silver and gold,
16:12for he was the high priest’s son-in-law.
16:13His heart was lifted up, and he wished to gain control of the country. He plotted deceitfully against Simon and his sons to remove them.

16:14Simon was visiting the cities in the country and attending to their care. He came down to Jericho with his sons Mattathias and Judas in the one hundred and seventy-seventh year, in the eleventh month, which is the month of Shebat.
16:15The son of Abubus deceitfully received them in the small stronghold called Dok, which he had built. He made a great drinking feast for them and hid men there.
16:16When Simon and his sons had become drunk, Ptolemy and his men arose, took their weapons, entered the banquet room against Simon, and killed him, his two sons, and some of his attendants.
16:17He committed a great act of treachery and repaid evil for good.
16:18Ptolemy wrote these things and sent them to the king, asking him to send forces to help him and hand over their country and cities.
16:19He sent others to Gazara to remove John, and sent letters to the commanders of thousands to come to him so that he might give them silver, gold, and gifts.
16:20He sent others to seize Jerusalem and the temple mountain.
16:21Someone ran ahead and reported to John at Gazara that his father and brothers had perished, and said, “He has also sent men to kill you.”
16:22When he heard, he was greatly astonished. He seized the men who had come to destroy him and killed them, for he had learned that they were seeking to destroy him.
16:23The rest of John’s deeds, his wars, the brave acts he performed, the building of the walls he built, and his actions—
16:24behold, these are written in the book of the days of his high priesthood, from the time he became high priest after his father.
